title: Pittsburgh Musicians Club and a Roy Eldridge story
summary: On the road she visited the Musicians Club where Roy Eldridge was in town, showing how many good players Pittsburgh had.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x:
And as I said before, there was an awful lot of music around Pittsburgh. There was the Musicians Club in downtown Pittsburgh. In fact, it was up on the hill, what they called The Hill in Pittsburgh, Wylie Avenue, where all the musicians would hang out when they'd get off their jobs. And the musicians would come up there -- this was really crazy -- when an out-of-town band would come into Pittsburgh they were usually invited to the Musicians Club, they called it Celebrity Night and the local musicians, their instruments would be sitting around, you know, and as soon as the guests -- it was murder when the guests would come because these cats would go and get their axes and start cutting the star.
I remember in particular, I was in Pittsburgh at the same time as Erskine Hawkins, Erskine Hawkins was playing at a dance hall, The Savoy Ballroom in Pittsburgh and I was appearing at one of the theaters there, so we were both invited

Roy Eldridge was in town that night. He had just left -- he walked away from the band, Gene Krupa's band and so he happened to be in there and oh, they insisted. Erskine tried to bow out of it, but, no, they wouldn't have it and as soon as he pulled out his horn, then everybody grabbed for their instrument and oh, oh, it was murder!
But you know, it was all in fun.
That would be late in the '30s, of course.
Oh, yes, this would be in the '50s, I guess.
Yeah, that late. Yes. Because I was on the road -- theaters, you know, I was still doing theaters at this time.
But what I'm driving at is that there were a lot of good musicians around Pittsburgh as you
